name: Inline Context – Footnotes, Tooltips & Glossary Notes
author: Joop Laan

sections.description:
Add footnotes, tooltips and glossary notes to any text in the block editor. A reader clicks a term, the explanation opens in place, and they carry on reading – no jump to the bottom of the page, no new tab.

Try it in your browser – a real WordPress with the plugin already set up. Nothing to install.

Built for sites with a lot of text: editorial, research, documentation and education.

How it works

  1. Select text in the block editor and press Cmd+Shift+I.
  2. Write the note. Rich text, links and images are supported.
  3. Optionally give it a category, with its own icon and colour.
  4. Publish. The note opens inline or as a tooltip, whichever you choose.

Mark a note reusable and it joins your Notes Library. Edit it once and every post that uses it updates.

Add the Glossary block to a page and those same notes are listed as a browsable reference – no second copy to keep in step with the first.

Key Features

  • Two display modes – an inline panel or a tooltip, with smart positioning and optional hover activation.
  • Reusable notes – a Notes Library showing each note’s usage count and the posts it appears in, searchable from inside the editor.
  • Glossary page – a block, or the [inline_context_glossary] shortcode, listing your notes on a page you choose, grouped A-Z or by category.
  • Categories – as many as you like, each with its own icon and colour. On WordPress 7.1 icons are drawn as SVG, picked from a curated set; any of the 300+ Dashicons still works too.
  • Styling without CSS – five WCAG 2.1 AA colour presets, plus live-preview control of colours, spacing, borders and shadows.
  • Images in notes – inserted straight from the Media Library.
  • Deep links – every note has its own anchor and opens automatically when someone follows that link.
  • Print – every note becomes a numbered footnote, listed at the foot of the page with a link back to its place in the text.
  • Keyboard shortcuts – Cmd+Shift+I to insert, Cmd+Shift+K to edit the note under the cursor.
  • Settings backup – export and import your configuration as JSON.

Accessibility

Operable by keyboard throughout, with full ARIA state, Escape to close, and focus returned to where it started. Note content is sanitised with DOMPurify.

If JavaScript does not run, the notes fall back to a numbered endnote list at the foot of the post, each with a link back to its place in the text, so the content stays reachable either way.

Translation-ready.

Credits & source

Built with visual artist Renée Kool, who wanted a single link to reveal several related sources. The model was the Dutch journalism platform De Correspondent – see their inline notes in this article.

Full source, including uncompiled JS and CSS: codeberg.org/joop/inline-context
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/inline-context, or install via the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Configure categories and styling under Settings → Inline Context.
  4. In the Block Editor, select text and click Inline Context.
  5. Add your note content and choose a category (optional).
sections.faq:
Can I use this for footnotes, sidenotes or a glossary?

All three – they are the same feature with different settings. Inline mode reads as a sidenote, tooltip mode as a glossary pop-up, and without JavaScript every note is numbered as a footnote at the end of the post. Reusable notes give you a glossary you edit in one place, and the Glossary block puts that same set of notes on a page readers can browse.

How do I add a glossary page?

Create a page, add the Glossary block, and publish. By default it lists your reusable notes grouped by first letter, with an A-Z jump bar. In the sidebar you can group by category instead, restrict it to chosen categories, include one-off notes, hide notes nothing links to yet, and show links to the posts each note explains. Those links go to the note’s own place in the article, not the top of it, and the note opens as the reader arrives.

If you would rather not use the block – in a widget, a template, or the Classic Editor – [inline_context_glossary] takes the same options: group_by="letter|category|none", categories="definition,source", only_reusable="true", show_usage="false", hide_unused="false", show_icons="true", show_jump_bar="true" and heading_level="2".

Every term gets its own id, so you can link straight to one: /glossary/#glossary-your-term.

Does this work with the Classic Editor?

Not for writing the notes into your text. Attaching a note to a phrase is a Block Editor format, and it has no Classic Editor equivalent – that part needs Gutenberg.

The rest does work. The Notes Library runs on a classic edit screen by design, so reusable notes can be written and organised there, and [inline_context_glossary] renders wherever a shortcode does, Classic Editor posts included. So a Classic Editor site can keep a glossary page; what it cannot do is anchor a note to a phrase mid-sentence.

Does it work with page builders like Elementor or Divi?

Notes are created in the block editor, so you cannot insert one from a page builder’s own editing screen. Notes already in your content display normally on the front end, whatever renders the page, and [inline_context_glossary] works in any builder that accepts shortcodes.

Does it work with caching and optimisation plugins?

Yes. If notes jump to the bottom of the page instead of opening, you are on a version before 2.8.2, where a plugin that delayed or deferred JavaScript could stop the script running. Update, or exclude inline-context/build/frontend.js from JavaScript delay and defer.

What happens to my notes if I deactivate the plugin?

Nothing is lost. The note text stays in the post and comes back when you reactivate. If you uninstall, the uninstaller can optionally strip the markup and leave your text clean.

Is it accessible?

Yes. Triggers are operable by keyboard with full ARIA state and Escape to close, and focus returns to where it started. If JavaScript does not run, the notes appear as a numbered endnote list at the foot of the post, each linking back to its place in the text.

Will it slow my site down?

No. A note’s content is stored with the post, so showing one costs no extra database queries.

Can notes contain images and links?

Yes. Notes accept rich text, links, and images from the Media Library. Images can be switched off under Settings if you want text-only notes.

Can I use the same note in several posts?

Yes. Mark it reusable and edit it once – every post that uses it updates.

Can I change the styles?

Yes. Pick one of five accessible colour presets, or set colours, spacing, borders and shadows yourself under Settings → Inline Context → Styling, with a live preview.

Is there a limit to the number of categories?

No. Create as many categories as your content structure requires.

Can I use any Dashicon?

Yes. You can type any Dashicon class name to use all 300+ icons.

What are the SVG category icons?

On WordPress 7.1 and later the plugin ships a curated set of icons drawn as SVG instead of as glyphs from the Dashicons font. They sit correctly on the text baseline in any theme, and once no category uses a Dashicon the font is no longer loaded on the front end at all. Pick one from the grid on a category’s screen. Existing categories keep their Dashicons until you choose to switch, and Settings offers to move over the ones that have an exact match.
sections.changelog:
2.9.1 – October 19, 2026

  • FIX: Printing a page now produces real footnotes. Every note is numbered where it appears and printed at the foot of the page, with a link back to its place in the text
  • FIX: Printing used to show only the notes a reader happened to have open, and no list at all. The notes it could not show still got a number, pointing at nothing
  • FIX: The chevron no longer prints, and a note left open on screen no longer prints in its open-state colour

2.9.0 – October 18, 2026

  • NEW: Glossary block, with an [inline_context_glossary] shortcode that takes the same options, listing your notes on a page you choose
  • NEW: Glossary entries group by first letter or by category, with an A-Z jump bar, and every term and group heading can be linked to directly
  • NEW: Glossary options for filtering to chosen categories, including one-off notes as well as reusable ones, hiding notes nothing links to, and linking to the posts each note explains – straight to the note’s own place in the article, where it opens as the reader arrives
  • NEW: Category icons can be drawn as SVG on WordPress 7.1 and later, from a curated set of twelve, instead of as glyphs from the Dashicons font
  • NEW: Visual icon picker on the category screen; the text field still accepts any Dashicons class
  • NEW: Settings offers to switch categories with an exact match over to SVG, lists the ones that have no equivalent, and changes nothing until asked
  • IMPROVED: SVG icons are centred on the font’s real cap height, so they sit correctly in any theme. Measured across four themes they land within 0.001em of the text’s optical centre, where Dashicons ranged from 0.012em to 0.040em depending on the theme
  • IMPROVED: The Dashicons font is no longer loaded on the front end once every category uses an SVG icon
  • IMPROVED: New sites on WordPress 7.1 start with SVG icons rather than being offered a conversion straight away
  • NOTE: Nothing changes on upgrade. Existing categories keep the icons they have, on any WordPress version, until you switch them over

2.8.3 – October 17, 2026

  • FIX: The editor popover opened at the far left of the screen instead of next to the text it belongs to, on WordPress 6.3 and later
  • FIX: Reusable notes showed a formatting toolbar over content that cannot be edited there; the panel now reads as the preview it is
  • FIX: Cmd+Shift+I did nothing when the cursor was inside an existing note. It now opens that note, as well as creating one from a selection
  • IMPROVED: The two links in the reusable-note panel each carry an icon, so it is clear which one opens a new tab and which copies to the clipboard
  • FIX: The note editor’s help text showed the literal characters </> instead of the code icon </> it was describing
  • FIX: Note excerpts in the editor’s “search existing notes” panel ended in … instead of an ellipsis; the same escape sequence was also returned by the Abilities API
  • FIX: Icon placement “middle” in the repository now matches the value WordPress.org has shipped since 2.7.2, so the released plugin and the source agree. Nothing changes in how notes look
  • DEV: New tooling for contributors – a one-command local WordPress environment, a demo-content seeder, a screenshot capture script, and an SVG source for the plugin banner
  • DEV: The canonical repository moved to Codeberg

2.8.2 – August 27, 2026

  • FIX: The “Notes” fallback section could stay visible at the bottom of posts, with clicks on a note jumping down to it instead of expanding in place. The frontend script tied its startup to DOMContentLoaded, so it never ran when a caching or optimization plugin deferred, delayed or combined the bundle until after that event had already fired
  • FIX: Accessibility — the fallback section was hidden by the generic js class, which Twenty Twenty, Seventeen, Sixteen and Fifteen add to the page themselves. On those themes the fallback was hidden even when this plugin’s script had not run, leaving screen reader and keyboard users pointed at a hidden anchor with no way to reach the note text. Hiding is now tied to the plugin’s own initialisation, so the fallback stays in place until the notes genuinely work
  • IMPROVED: Confirmed WordPress 7.1 compatibility — “Tested up to” header bumped to 7.1
  • DEV: Added a @wordpress/env configuration and npm run env:* scripts for a one-command local WordPress environment
  • DEV: Added tests/test-frontend.php covering the endnotes fallback and its accessibility guarantees
  • DEV: uninstall.php now removes every plugin option, not just three of them

2.8.1 – May 2, 2026

  • FIX: Inline context popover no longer closes when inserting an image from the WordPress Media Library

2.8.0 – May 2, 2026

  • NEW: Embed images inside inline context notes via the WordPress Media Library
  • NEW: Image button in the note editor toolbar (shown when image support is enabled)
  • NEW: “Allow images in notes” admin setting in the General tab (default: enabled)
  • NEW: Custom Quill image blot preserves alt, loading, decoding, and class attributes
  • NEW: inline_context_allowed_image_protocols filter for sites that need data URIs or other schemes
  • NEW: Three CSS variables for image sizing customization (tooltip max width/height, inline max height)
  • IMPROVED: Tooltip mode caps images at ~280×200 to keep tooltips compact
  • IMPROVED: Inline mode caps image height at 400px while allowing full content width
  • IMPROVED: Print styles handle images with page-break avoidance and sensible sizing
  • IMPROVED: Confirmed WordPress 7.0 compatibility — “Tested up to” bumped to 7.0
  • IMPROVED: Always sets alt=”” on images missing alt text so screen readers don’t announce filenames
  • IMPROVED: Image src restricted to http(s) and relative paths by default for security
  • IMPROVED: Settings export/import now includes the image-support toggle

2.7.3 – March 21, 2026

  • FIX: Category icons now align correctly with text at all icon placement settings
  • FIX: Category icon double-scaling issue causing icons to render at half the intended size

2.7.2 – March 20, 2026

  • FIX: Tooltip hover mode no longer shows erratic show/hide behavior
  • FIX: Admin settings JS toggles now work (display mode, link style, preset warnings)
  • NEW: Icon right margin CSS variable for theme.json and admin settings
  • IMPROVED: Refactored icon rendering to use consistent HTML elements for both default and category icons
  • IMPROVED: Fine-tuned icon placement values for top, middle, and bottom positions
  • IMPROVED: Pill style always centers icons regardless of placement setting

2.7.1 – December 30, 2025

  • IMPROVED: Smart link URL display in print (shows URLs except for anchor links)

  • NEW: Color preset system with five pre-configured professional color schemes
  • NEW: Modern Blue (Default), Minimalist Gray, High Contrast, Warm Earth Tones, and Dark Mode presets

  • IMPROVED: Documentation

For complete version history, see changelog.txt
